h1: The 8 Best Video Intercom Systems for Homes and Small Apartment Buildings, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Video Intercom Systems 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 8 video intercom systems compared on wired or WiFi setup, monitor size, door release, access control and apartment use.
summary: The LUMOBELL is the most complete single-family system here, with a 7 inch touchscreen, a 1080P camera and support for a 12V electric door lock. The Aiphone JOS-1VW is the premium pick for reliability, the ACEBELL is the easiest to install thanks to WiFi, and the AMOCAM suits a small apartment building. The TMEZON is the cheap way into wired video.
intro: The first mistake with a video intercom is choosing it for the screen. The screen is the easy part. The decisions that cause regret are wired versus WiFi, whether the system can release your door, and how many indoor monitors you can add later. Pick wrong, and you are either drilling through walls or living with a lagging connection.

This ranking is organised around those choices. We reviewed eight systems from their listings and published specs, covering display size, camera resolution, lock support, access control and the number of monitors or units each handles. Where the listing says nothing about a feature, we do not assume it exists.

products.name: LUMOBELL Wired Video Doorbell Intercom System
products.verdict: A wired 7 inch touchscreen kit with a 1080P camera and electric lock support.
products.description:
The LUMOBELL is a wired intercom with a 7 inch HD touchscreen monitor, a 1080P door camera and support for a 12V electric door lock, in the $100 to $200 bracket. That combination covers what most single-family homes need: see the visitor, talk, and release the gate or door.

It wins because it packs the full workflow into one affordable kit. A wired link avoids the dropped calls that plague WiFi doorbells, and the touchscreen is easier for relatives to use than a button panel. It loses points only because wired installation means running cable, and the lock support applies to 12V locks, so you must confirm your lock type first.

Buy it if you are building or renovating and can run a cable to the door. Skip it if the walls are finished and you cannot pull wire.
pros: 7 inch touchscreen is easy to use
cons: Needs cable run to the door
products.idealFor: Homeowners who can run cable and want a full kit.
products.skipIf: You cannot run wiring through finished walls.

products.name: Aiphone JOS-1VW Video Intercom Box Set
products.verdict: A metal door station with a 7 inch WiFi monitor from a long-standing intercom maker.
products.description:
The JOS-1VW is a box set pairing a 7 inch WiFi monitor with a metal door station, in the $500+ bracket. Aiphone is a specialist intercom brand rather than a general electronics seller, and that history is the main reason buyers choose it.

It ranks second because it competes on build rather than price. A metal door station resists weather and tampering better than a plastic one, and the set is sold as a complete package. The reason it is not first is simple: it costs several times what the LUMOBELL does for a similar-sounding feature list, and the listing gives few extra specs to justify the premium on paper.

Choose it if you want a brand known for dependable intercoms and you are willing to pay for it. Skip it if budget decides.
pros: Complete box set in one purchase
cons: Little extra detail on the listing
products.idealFor: Buyers who want an established intercom brand.
products.skipIf: A lower price matters more than brand.

products.name: AMOCAM Apartment Video Intercom System
products.verdict: A video doorbell system built for four households in a small apartment building.
products.description:
The AMOCAM is a four-unit household video intercom with a video doorbell, in the $200 to $500 bracket. It addresses a case most single-home kits ignore: one entrance serving several separate apartments.

It ranks third because multi-unit capability is rare in this price tier. Each household gets its own indoor monitor, which means visitors can call the right flat instead of ringing everyone. It sits behind the top two on polish, since the listing is brief on camera resolution and lock options, so confirm those before buying.

It suits landlords and small multi-family homes. Skip it if you only need one indoor monitor.
pros: Serves four households from one door
Visitors can call the right unit
products.idealFor: Small multi-unit buildings sharing one entrance.
products.skipIf: You only need a single indoor monitor.

products.name: Smart Video Doorbell Intercom System with 600lb Magnetic Lock
products.verdict: Bundles a 600lb magnetic lock, RFID card access and app unlock in one package.
products.description:
This package combines a video doorbell intercom with a 600lb magnetic lock, RFID IC card access and remote unlock through the Tuya app, in the $200 to $500 bracket. It goes beyond viewing the visitor and handles who can come in.

It ranks fourth because it is a complete access-control package rather than just an intercom. RFID cards let residents or staff enter without a call, and the app lets you open the door remotely. The compromise is that it is more complex to install than a basic kit, and the lock suits specific door types, so check the frame before ordering.

Pick it for a gate, shop back door or shared entrance where card access matters. Skip it if you only want a doorbell with a screen.
products.idealFor: Shared entrances and gates that need card access.
products.skipIf: You want a basic doorbell with a screen.

products.name: Wired Video Doorbell Apartment Intercom System, 1 Camera and 2 Monitors
products.verdict: One door camera feeding two 7 inch touchscreen monitors with remote unlock.
products.description:
This kit pairs one camera with two 7 inch touchscreen monitors and supports remote unlock, in the $200 to $500 bracket. It is built for homes where more than one room needs to answer the door.

It ranks fifth because the second monitor is the real feature. A downstairs unit and a bedroom or office unit mean you do not have to run to the front hall every time. Against the LUMOBELL it adds a screen but offers fewer stated details, such as camera resolution, and the brand is generic.

It works for two-floor homes and shared workspaces. Skip it if one monitor is enough, since the LUMOBELL gives you a clearer spec sheet for less.
pros: Two indoor monitors in the kit
products.idealFor: Two-floor homes needing two answering points.
products.skipIf: A single monitor is all you need.

products.name: ACEBELL Wireless Smart Video Doorbell Intercom System
products.verdict: WiFi, a 1080P camera and no subscription, with no cable to run.
products.description:
The ACEBELL is a WiFi video doorbell intercom with a 1080P camera and no subscription, in the $100 to $200 bracket. Its appeal is simple: you can set it up without pulling cable through a wall.

It ranks sixth because WiFi trades convenience for dependability. A wireless link can lag or drop when the signal is weak, which is the exact moment you are trying to answer the door. The no-subscription claim is a genuine money saver compared with cloud-based doorbells, but the listing says little about lock support.

It is a good fit for renters and finished homes. Skip it if you need a rock-solid wired link or electric lock release.
products.idealFor: Renters and finished homes that cannot take new wiring.
products.skipIf: You need electric lock release or a wired link.

products.name: TMEZON Wired Video Intercom System
products.verdict: A 7 inch wired video intercom with unlock support for the least money.
products.description:
The TMEZON is a wired 7 inch video intercom that supports unlock, in the $50 to $100 bracket. It delivers the core function of seeing, talking and releasing the door for the lowest price here.

It ranks seventh because savings come with a thinner spec list. The listing does not give camera resolution or monitor features, so you are buying on the basics. It still beats a wired doorbell with no screen, and it is a reasonable starter for a garage gate or a rental unit.

It makes sense for a tight budget. Skip it if you want a stated camera resolution or extra access features.
products.idealFor: Budget buyers wanting wired video and unlock.
products.skipIf: You want clear camera specs or extra features.

products.name: Panasonic Door Intercom White
products.verdict: A basic video and audio door intercom from a known brand, at a premium price.
products.description:
The Panasonic is a door intercom with basic video and audio, in the $500+ bracket. It is a straightforward system from a household-name brand.

It ranks last because the price does not match the stated features. The listing describes only basic video and audio, with no resolution, screen size or lock support, while far cheaper kits here list those details. You pay for the name.

It can suit a buyer who prizes brand familiarity and has simple needs. Skip it if you want measurable specs for the money.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want a familiar brand and simple use.
products.skipIf: You need stated specs or access features.

whatMatters.detail: A wired system uses a cable from the door station to the monitor, so the picture does not depend on your network. WiFi systems skip the cable but can lag when the signal weakens. Check the listing for connection type and test your signal at the door before buying a wireless unit.

Many intercoms can trigger an electric strike or magnetic lock, but only specific types. The LUMOBELL lists 12V lock support. Confirm your lock voltage and type before ordering, because a mismatch means the intercom cannot open the door.

A 7 inch screen is comfortable for older eyes and easy to read at a glance. Some kits include two monitors for multi-floor homes. Count where you want to answer the door, and compare against the monitors in the box.

A 1080P camera is enough to recognise a face, while unlisted resolutions are a gamble. Look for a stated figure on the listing, and prefer kits that publish one. Night vision and angle details are useful extras when listed.

RFID cards and app unlock let residents enter without a call and let you open the door remotely. They matter for shared entrances and gates. Check which app and card system the listing names, and whether it adds a separate setup.

howToChoose.intro: Decide wired or wireless first, because it determines installation effort and reliability.

cards.label: Wired

cards.label: WiFi
cards.text: Setup is faster and needs no new cable, which helps renters. The ACEBELL and the Aiphone use wireless links, which can lag if the signal at the door is poor.

howToChoose.note: Choose wired whenever you can run cable. WiFi is the default only when you cannot.

faq.q: Can a video intercom open my door?
faq.a: Yes, if it supports your lock type. The LUMOBELL lists 12V electric lock support, and the magnetic lock bundle includes its own lock. Confirm the voltage and lock style before ordering.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake when buying one?
faq.a: Picking a WiFi model without checking the signal at the door. A weak connection causes lag when someone rings. Test your signal first, or choose a wired kit.

faq.q: Is the Aiphone worth it over cheaper kits?
faq.a: It is worth it if you value a specialist brand and a metal door station for years of use. On stated features alone, the LUMOBELL offers similar basics for far less. Decide whether the brand premium matters to you.

Wired kits need a cable from the door to the monitor and a power source, which is easiest during construction or renovation. WiFi kits mount and pair through an app. Magnetic lock bundles need a suitable door frame.

faq.q: Do these systems need a subscription?
faq.a: The ACEBELL lists no subscription, and wired kits generally work without one. App-based systems like the Tuya package may use a free app. Read the listing for any cloud features.

faq.q: Can I add more monitors later?
faq.a: It depends on the system. The two-monitor kit and the AMOCAM already include multiple screens, while single-monitor sets may accept extras only from the same maker. Check expansion options before you buy.

finalTake: Buy the LUMOBELL if you can run cable and want the most complete home system for the money. Choose the Aiphone JOS-1VW for a premium metal door station, the ACEBELL when you cannot run wire, and the AMOCAM for a small apartment building. For gates and card entry, the magnetic lock bundle is the one to get.
